'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign]]
*****Secretary-General [[Arsenio Dominguez]] says that the [[International Maritime Organization]] will pause an evacuation effort for 11,000 seafarers on stranded ships in the [[Strait of Hormuz]] after [[Iran]] objected to the plan and after a vessel was attacked near [[Oman]]. [https://www.axios.com/2026/06/25/iran-ship-attacked-strait-hormuz-un-sailors-evacuation-paused (''Axios'')] [https://www.nbcnews.com/world/iran/oil-tanker-passes-strait-hormuz-iran-threats-traffic-trump-tolls-oman-rcna351704 (NBC News)] 
*****The [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy|Navy]] rejects [[United Nations]]-backed temporary shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz proposed with [[Oman]] while negotiations continue over the waterway's future administration. [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/25/oil-price-supply-concerns-ease-with-hormuz-tanker-traffic-resuming-.html (CNBC)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jun/25/un-backed-plan-ships-trapped-strait-of-hormuz-rejected-iran (''The Guardian'')]
*****[[Singapore]]-[[Port of registry|flagged]] [[container ship]] ''Ever Lovely'' is damaged after being struck by a unknown projectile off the coast of Oman, near Dahit in the [[Musandam Governorate]]. No casualties are reported. [https://theedgemalaysia.com/node/808362 (''The Edge Malaysia'')] [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/25/iran-ghalibaf-trump-us-farm-products-assets.html (CNBC)]
****[[Foreign Ministry (Oman)|Omani foreign minister]] [[Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi]] confirms that no transit fees would be imposed on ships using the Strait of Hormuz as part of future management of the waterway. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2648575/middle-east (''Arab News'')]
****Two [[liquefied natural gas]] [[LNG carrier|carriers]] from [[Qatar]], the [[Marshall Islands]]-flagged ''Bu Samra'' bound for the [[Far East]], and the [[Liberia]]-flagged ''Patris'', transit through the Strait of Hormuz after being stranded for a period of time since the waterway was closed. [https://menafn.com/1111311047/Qatari-LNG-Tankers-Resume-Hormuz-Transit-as-US-Iran-Tensions-Recede (MENAFN)]
**[[2026 Lebanon war]]
***[[France–Italy relations]], [[France–Lebanon relations]], [[Italy–Lebanon relations]]
****[[France]] and [[Italy]] agree to establish a multinational coalition to support [[Lebanon]] after the [[United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon]] ends its mission on 31 December 2026. The initiative aims to strengthen [[Lebanese Armed Forces|Lebanon's armed forces]] and maintain [[international security]] support. [https://english.news.cn/europe/20260626/941c459c6657426c920a8c9b411fc841/c.html (Xinhua)]
***[[Israel]] and Lebanon deny a claim from a [[United States]] official that some [[Israeli Ground Forces|Israeli troops]] have been withdrawn from [[southern Lebanon]] as a goodwill gesture during [[2026 Israel–Lebanon peace talks|their negotiations]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jun/25/un-backed-plan-ships-trapped-strait-of-hormuz-rejected-iran (''The Guardian'')] 
**[[Minister of Defense (Israel)|Israeli defense minister]] [[Israel Katz]] says that [[Israel Defense Forces|the military]] will keep troops in occupied Lebanon, [[Syria]], and [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]] in [[State of Palestine|Palestine]] forever. [https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20260625-israel-will-remain-in-territory-occupied-in-lebanon-syria-gaza-indefinitely-defence-minister/ (AA via ''Middle East Monitor'')]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Darfur campaign (2023–present)|Darfur campaign]], [[Darfur genocide (2023–present)|Darfur genocide]]
***The [[International Organization for Migration]] reports that 1,430 people were displaced from five villages in [[Sudan]]'s [[North Darfur]] [[States of Sudan|state]] in a single day due to worsening insecurity. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/over-1-400-displaced-in-sudans-north-darfur-in-single-day-un/3978408 (AA)]
**Two people are killed and seven others are injured in a [[drone warfare|drone strike]] by the [[paramilitary]] group [[Rapid Support Forces]] on a [[Filling station|fuel station]] in [[Rabak]], [[White Nile State|White Nile]]. [https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20260625-2-killed-7-injured-in-rsf-drone-strike-on-fuel-station-in-southern-sudan-medics/?amp (AA via ''Middle East Monitor'')]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**Three gunmen and a [[National Guard (Mexico)|National Guard]] officer are killed in an attempted ambush on the outskirts of [[Acapulco]], [[Guerrero]]. [https://www.proceso.com.mx/nacional/estados/2026/6/25/emboscada-a-la-guardia-nacional-en-acapulco-deja-cuatro-muertos-374752.html (''Proceso'' <small>in Spanish</small>)]
**Patricia Negrete Tafoya, a ''[[Madres buscadoras|madre buscadora]]'', is shot dead upon leaving from work in [[Pénjamo]], [[Guanajuato]], marking the fifth killing of activists in the last four months. [https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/06/25/politica/buscadoras-condenan-asesinato-de-patricia-negrete-en-guanajuato-suman-cinco-activistas-ultimadas (''La Jornada'' <small>in Spanish</small>)]
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**Two [[National Police of Colombia|police]] officers are killed and four others are others injured after [[FARC dissidents]] attack a police post in [[Calima, Valle del Cauca|Calima]], [[Valle del Cauca Department|Valle del Cauca]]. [https://caracol.com.co/2026/06/24/dos-policias-fueron-asesinados-en-medio-de-enfrentamientos-en-calima-el-darien-en-el-valle-del-cauca (''El Tiempo'' <small>in Spanish</small>)]
*[[France–Russia relations]]
**[[President of France|French president]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] announces that [[French Navy|the navy]] intercepted and boarded the [[Cameroon]]-flagged, [[Russia]]-[[Russian shadow fleet|linked]] [[oil]] [[Tanker (ship)|tanker]] ''Deliver'' off the coast of [[Sicily]], Italy, two days earlier. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/06/25/france-intercepts-shadow-fleet-tanker-near-sicily-a93096 (''The Moscow Times'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war]]
**[[Economy of the United States]]
***The [[Federal Reserve]] [[inflation]] rises to a three-year high in [[2026#May|May]]. Additionally, the [[United States Department of Commerce|U.S. Department of Commerce]] reported a 4.1% increase in consumer prices driven by high gas prices, the largest since [[2021–2023 inflation surge|April 2023]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/25/business/inflation-iran-war-prices.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
***[[Reuters]] reports that, over the past week, [[crude oil]] [[Maritime shipping|shipments]] through the Strait of Hormuz have risen to their highest level since the start of the war, but traffic still remains a fraction of pre-war levels. [https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/6/26/oil-prices-climb-after-attack-in-strait-of-hormuz-halts-evacuation-plan (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/crude-shipments-through-hormuz-highest-since-war-amid-concerns-over-iran-exit-2026-06-25/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 European heatwaves]]
**A monitoring system in [[Spain]] estimates that a [[heat wave]] contributed to 212 deaths between Sunday and Wednesday. The country also records [[List of extreme temperatures in Spain|its highest average June temperatures]] since at least 1950. [https://www.nst.com.my/world/world/2026/06/1472584/heatwave-linked-212-deaths-spain-sunday-wednesday-public-institute (AFP via ''New Straits Times'')]
**[[Switzerland]] and the [[United Kingdom]] both record their [[List of weather records|hottest ever temperatures]] in June with a provisional high of 36.7°C (98.06F), recorded in [[Somerset]], [[England]], and a temperature of 38°C recorded by a [[weather station]] in [[Basel]], Switzerland. [https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/jun/25/highest-june-minimum-temperature-record-broken-cardiff-savage-heatwave-continues (''The Guardian'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Immigration detention in the second Trump administration]]
**[[Governor of Florida|Florida governor]] [[Ron DeSantis]] confirms that the [[Alligator Alcatraz]] [[Immigration detention in the United States|detention center]] in [[Ochopee, Florida|Ochopee]], [[Florida]], U.S., will close operations, a year after it opened. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/united-states/alligator-alcatraz-detention-centre-shuts-in-us-official (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')] [https://www.politico.com/news/2026/06/25/alligator-alcatraz-officially-shutters-florida-desantis-homan-00976165 (''Politico'')]
*[[Somalia–United States relations]]
**Abdikerm Abdelahi Eidleh, a central suspect in the [[Feeding Our Future]] [[Child health and nutrition in Africa|child nutrition]] aid [[fraud]] scheme, is apprehended in [[Mogadishu]], [[Somalia]]. The U.S. [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]] says he fled the country in 2022 and evaded prosecution for more than four years before his capture. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/6/27/somali-intelligence-helps-us-arrest-alleged-ringleader-of-minnesota-fraud (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.cnn.com/2026/06/26/us/minnesota-fraud-custody-eidleh (AP via CNN)] [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/minnesota-fraud-arrest-somalia-abdikerm-eidleh/ (CBS News)]
*[[Turkey|Turkish]] [[General Directorate of Security (Turkey)|police]] seize more than 10,000 [[History of Turkey|historical]] artifacts during a raid on a residence in [[Istanbul]] and arrest two people in connection with an investigation into the alleged [[Looted art|illegal possession of cultural property]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2648571/amp (AFP via ''Arab News'')]
